title: Observed flood-change and recovery
notes: All plotted regional comparisons use the same pixels valid on every selected date or pair. Per-date coverage is shown separately; missing coverage is never reported as zero change.
Backscatter changes can reflect moisture, vegetation, roughness or geometry; they do not identify a cause by themselves.
Water candidates use a user-controlled threshold. They require local independent validation; shadow and smooth dry ground can be mistaken for water.
Area uses the common valid analysis grid; local UTM areas are approximate. Coarse analysis cells are averages, not new high-resolution observations.
Dated water playback uses the same common valid footprint and threshold on every date; it shows candidates, not verified floods or daily water evolution.

Baseline is the median backscatter of observations before the comparison date. Automatic comparison selection finds the largest consecutive candidate expansion; it does not verify a flood. Last-wet and first-dry observations bound the first observed return to dry; intervening wet/dry cycles are unknown, and no later dry observation means unresolved, not still flooded.
Input is a local native-grid area extract, not a complete original NASA product; only the saved rectangle can be analyzed.
GCOV source-sample mask is applied before averaging. It is not a terrain-shadow or water classifier.

tracking.meaning: Dated candidate objects linked by overlap on a common analysis grid. Gaps are unobserved; links do not establish uninterrupted physical identity.

threshold_sensitivity.description: Five user-threshold scenarios on identical support. This is sensitivity, not a confidence interval.

observation_gaps.meaning: Intervals without an acquisition are unobserved, not unchanged.

result_passport.interpretation: Dark radar returns are water candidates, not confirmed flooding. Two dates cannot establish onset, duration or recovery.
result_passport.validation: Engineering reproducibility and checksum checks are separate from independent scientific validation. Read the case-study comparison.

report.headline: What these observations show
findings: 2 compatible GCOV observations cover 2026-01-05 to 2026-01-17. Regional comparisons use 59,392 common analysis cells (593.920 km²).
Between first and last observations, candidate water gained 90.470 km² and lost 14.980 km² on the same footprint.
Comparison observation: 2026-01-17 (user comparison date). New candidate water: 90.470 km²; later observed dry: 0.000 km²; unresolved: 90.470 km².
report.comparison_basis: fixed common footprint across all selected observations
next_checks: Inspect observation counts and source quality before interpreting a pattern.
Compare the map and observed dates; blank pixels are missing evidence.
Use independent observations to test environmental attribution.
report.validation: Synthetic engineering tests check known calculations and missing-data behavior; independent real-world accuracy is not established.

reading_guide.measurement: A before/comparison-date test for newly appearing low-return water candidates, with later dry observations only where those dates exist.
reading_guide.colours: Category numbers are labels. New water means the rule changed from not-water in the baseline to water at the comparison date. Zero is a valid non-candidate result; transparency means missing evidence or a chosen display opacity.
reading_guide.checks: Check the same usable footprint, baseline and comparison dates, native support and threshold-sensitivity maps. Recovery requires later observations; no later dry observation is not proof that flooding continued.
reading_guide.cannot: This rule does not confirm inundation, isolate flooded vegetation, measure water depth, or establish exact onset, duration or recovery between acquisitions.
reading_guide.validation: Source checksums verify input integrity. Replay checks verify reproducibility. Neither establishes independent environmental accuracy for this run.
